challenge.name: The Locked Shadow
challenge.description: A supplier contract for the next promotion week is already signed, and the team cannot deploy the new model without a shadow run to verify it. #reliability_ruth# demands a fully automated and governed shadow environment to protect the live forecast, while #automation_alex# insists on keeping it manual to avoid breaking the current pipeline stability.
challenge.roundIntroduction: The nightly forecast job failed to generate suggestions for the northern stores because the shadow environment was not running. The buyer for the middle aisle promotion has already committed to the supplier, and any delay in validating the new model risks a stockout on the leaflet.

on_enter_ops.reason: The shadow environment was taken offline to free up compute for the promotion allocation run

stalemate_ops.reason: The pipeline step to trigger shadow runs was disabled to prevent further compute costs

roster.name: Automation Alex
roster.role: Builds automated ML pipelines to ensure seamless integration and deployment. Prioritizes reliable infrastructure for frequent software deployments. Maintains system operational stability and focuses on CI/CD tooling.
roster.priorities: Building automated pipelines and maintaining full system operational stability. Ensuring seamless deployment, integration, and stability of models and services in production.

roster.name: Requirements Reuben
roster.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.
roster.priorities: Guaranteeing high product quality through rigorous testing of applications. Guaranteeing the integrity, confidentiality, and security of all ML assets. Meeting internal and external compliance and data protection standards. Keeping infrastructure stable, reproducible, and cost-controlled.

roster.name: Reliability Ruth
roster.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.
roster.priorities: Pushes the delivery of reliable ML-powered features that directly improve the user experience. CI/CD and working feedback loops. Identifying and reporting issues to facilitate iterative improvements.

roster.name: Efficiency Emilia
roster.role: Uses deep domain knowledge to define business goals, objectives, and KPIs. Aligns ML features with overarching product strategy and organizational roadmaps. Evaluates system performance, operational capability, and project costs.
roster.priorities: Applying deep domain knowledge to ensure models fulfill specific business goals. Aligning ML solutions with clear objectives, KPIs, and business goals. Making organization-level decisions and enhancing overall operational capability. Defining products by defining and optimizing product features.

items.fact: {automation_alex} proposed wiring the registry hand-off straight through containerization into the shadow hand-off.

readings.driver: The more of that chain runs on its own, the fewer manual hops slow a new model down.
readings.boundary: He will not sign off on a release that still needs someone to trigger each hand-off by hand.
readings.trade_off: He would accept leaving one of those hand-offs manual if the rest moves on its own.
readings.fact: That is simply how the deployment chain is wired together today.

items.fact: {automation_alex} proposed keeping containerization capped at its current hands on setup for now.

readings.driver: Pushing containerization further would free him up to focus on the shadow hand-off instead.
readings.boundary: He will not let containerization slip below its current hands on setup.
readings.trade_off: He would accept containerization staying exactly as it runs today if the rest of the chain moves instead.
readings.fact: That is simply the ceiling containerization sits at right now.

items.fact: {automation_alex} proposed trading part of his automation budget for faster progress on the shadow hand-off.

readings.driver: Spending more of that budget elsewhere would speed up work the team actually notices.
readings.boundary: He will not give up his entire automation budget for one single hand-off.
readings.trade_off: He would give up part of his automation budget if the shadow hand-off moves forward.
readings.fact: That is simply how his automation budget is split up this cycle.

items.fact: {automation_alex} proposed leaving the hand-off into the gateway exactly as it runs today.

readings.driver: Automating that hand-off would free capacity for the bigger shadow deployment push.
readings.boundary: He will not accept that hand-off falling further behind its current setup.
readings.trade_off: He would accept that hand-off staying as it runs today if the shadow chain moves instead.
readings.fact: That is simply the state the gateway hand-off is in right now.

items.fact: {requirements_reuben} proposed moving the hand-off into orchestration off manual triggering.

readings.driver: The less anyone has to trigger that hand-off by hand, the fewer audit gaps show up later.
readings.boundary: He will not sign off on a release where that hand-off still needs a manual trigger.
readings.trade_off: He would accept that hand-off staying manual if the review paperwork around it gets simplified instead.
readings.fact: That is simply how the hand-off into orchestration runs today.

items.fact: {requirements_reuben} proposed leaving the pipeline's sign off step exactly as relaxed as it is today.

readings.driver: A stricter sign off step would catch issues before they reach the shadow run.
readings.boundary: He will not accept the pipeline shipping with no review step at all forever.
readings.trade_off: He would accept the pipeline keeping no formal review step if the shadow hand-off gets fixed first.
readings.fact: That is simply how little review the pipeline gets right now.

items.fact: {reliability_ruth} proposed that shadow deployment carry a formal sign off before anything ships through it.

readings.driver: A formal sign off would catch a bad model before it ever touches live traffic.
readings.boundary: She will not accept shadow deployment shipping without that formal sign off in place.
readings.trade_off: She would accept a lighter review if the sign off still covers the riskiest changes.
readings.fact: That is simply the review shadow deployment gets today, none at all.

items.fact: {reliability_ruth} proposed leaving canary testing exactly as it stands today.

readings.driver: Standing up canary testing would catch a bad model before shadow even sees it.
readings.boundary: She will not accept canary testing being removed from the roadmap entirely.
readings.trade_off: She would accept canary testing staying off the roadmap if shadow deployment gets fixed first.
readings.fact: That is simply the state canary testing is in today, not yet set up.

items.fact: {efficiency_emilia} proposed moving model serving fully onto automatic handling.

readings.driver: The less anyone has to touch serving by hand, the sooner promotion traffic gets handled.
readings.boundary: She will not accept serving staying hands on through the next promotion window.
readings.trade_off: She would accept serving staying hands on a while longer if the gateway hand-off improves instead.
readings.fact: That is simply how serving is run today, by hand.

items.fact: {efficiency_emilia} proposed giving the gateway its own automatic handling instead of leaving it as is.

readings.driver: The sooner that hand-off runs on its own, the faster traffic moves through the gateway.
readings.boundary: She will not accept the gateway staying manual through the next promotion window.
readings.trade_off: She would accept the gateway staying manual a while longer if serving gets automated first.
readings.fact: That is simply how the gateway is handled today, not automatically.

items.fact: {efficiency_emilia} proposed that the gateway carry a formal sign off before traffic reaches it.

readings.driver: A formal sign off on the gateway would catch a bad release before it reaches customers.
readings.boundary: She will not accept the gateway shipping traffic without that formal sign off in place.
readings.trade_off: She would accept a lighter check on the gateway if serving gets fully automated instead.
readings.fact: That is simply the sign off status the gateway has today, nothing formal yet.

items.fact: Shadow deployment is broken; nothing has used it in weeks.

readings.driver: Bringing it back would let every new model get validated before going live.
readings.boundary: Nobody will sign off on a release that skips that validation step entirely.
readings.trade_off: The team would accept delaying one release if it means getting that validation step back.
readings.fact: That is simply the state shadow deployment is in right now.

items.fact: Canary testing does not exist yet for the forecast model.

readings.driver: Standing it up would catch a bad model before it reaches every store.
readings.boundary: Nobody will sign off on skipping that safety net for good.
readings.trade_off: The team would accept skipping it once more if the bigger shadow fix lands first.
readings.fact: That is simply where canary testing stands today, not yet built.

items.fact: The hand-off from containerization into orchestration is still triggered by hand.

readings.driver: Automating that hand-off would free up time for the shadow deployment work instead.
readings.boundary: Nobody will accept that hand-off staying untested through the next release.
readings.trade_off: The team would accept that hand-off staying manual a while longer if shadow gets fixed first.
readings.fact: That is simply the current manual state of the hand-off into orchestration.
